item.text: {"text":"The TREC 2025 recommendation track, reported in 2026, separates functional substitutes, complements, objective compatibility, and subjective preference. Complementarity alone does not establish compatibility: a phone case complements phones but may fit only specific models. Implicit histories cannot reliably establish these nuanced relationships. For metadata-only diagnostics, this supports separate evidence fields for shared function, accessory relationship, and explicit model/interface constraints; missing specifications should remain unknown. Historical substitutes indicate possible redundancy, not proof of ownership or fulfilled need. [TREC overview](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.17138v1)\n\nSelective-prediction research distinguishes evidence sufficiency from confidence and correctness. *Sufficient Context* (ICLR 2025) improves selective answering by using both sufficiency and confidence signals; ReCoVERR (2024) investigates gathering evidence before abstaining. These findings concern question answering, so their application here is a proposed diagnostic adaptation: label explicit compatibility conflicts only when supported by quoted metadata; label possible fulfilled needs cautiously using functional overlap and timestamps; otherwise abstain from the diagnosis. Check these proxies against available qualitative feedback, separating explicit complaints from ambiguous or absent feedback. Report precision and coverage for each diagnostic label, with uncertainty intervals; sparse feedback supports exploratory agreement estimates, not reliable probability calibration. Never convert missing evidence into rejection or interpret abstention as a negative preference. Keep diagnostic abstention separate from the benchmark’s required rankings. [Sufficient Context](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/file/33dffa2e3d2ab74a783d1a8c292f66d9-Paper-Conference.pdf), [ReCoVERR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.15610)"}
